study_identification_part.si4_title: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize age-related effects of 16p11.2 copy number variants on brain structure across childhood, adolescence, and early adulthood using a large normative developmental dataset for accurate age adjustment and to determine when these alterations appear and whether they evolve with age.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: NIHPD (NIH MRI study of normal brain development)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The normative reference dataset is clearly stated as NIHPD Objective 1 data, which was used to model age- and sex-related brain growth trajectories.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the multi-site longitudinal data from Objective 1 (i.e. initial time-point for enrolment from 4.5 to 18.5 years) of the publicly available NIHPD project (Evans and Brain Development Cooperative, 2006).

rci2_hc_n.reason: The NIHPD normative model was built using data from 339 children who were scanned longitudinally, resulting in 874 total scans.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The normative model (Aubert-Broche et al., 2011) used data from 339 children (179 females and 160 males), scanned longitudinally at 2 or 3 time points, with approximately 24 months between scans and mean age at first scan of 11.0 years, for a total of 874 scans.

nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: we included both linear and quadratic effects of age in the fixed effects structure. caa2_diseases_studied.answer: 16p11.2 BP4-5 deletion; 16p11.2 BP4-5 duplication. Associated conditions include neurodevelopmental disorders such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability.
caa2_diseases_studied.reason: The study's primary focus is the 16p11.2 CNV. The abstract and introduction state these are linked to various neurodevelopmental disorders, which are detailed in Supplementary Table 1.
caa2_diseases_studied.supporting_text: 16p11.2 copy number variants (breakpoint 4 -5) confer high risk for neurodevelopmental disorders... and A total of 53 of 56 deletion carriers (95%) had at least one psychiatric diagnosis...15 of 19 duplication carriers (79%) had at least one psychiatric diagnosis

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Inverse gene dosage effects in global and regional brain measures for 16p11.2 CNV carriers are present by ~4.5 years and remain stable through early adulthood.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Deletion carriers showed higher Z-scores vs controls for total brain (mean Z=1.165, p<0.0001), gray (Z=0.414, p=0.00433) and white matter (Z=0.693, p<0.0001), whereas duplication carriers showed lower Z-scores (total brain Z=-1.17, p=0.0001; gray Z=-0.631, p=0.00272; white Z=-0.53, p=0.0018) and larger lateral ventricles (Z=1.629, p<0.0001). TBM revealed DEL>CTRL>DUP in bilateral calcarine cortex and insula, among others. No age*group interactions; effects stable across 4.5–23 years.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normalization approach enables cross-age analysis using external normative trajectories; authors suggest future refinements with 3T longitudinal data and alternative modeling (e.g., splines) to better capture variability.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Technical differences in MRI acquisition between the normative (1.5T) and clinical (3T, multi-site) datasets; limited statistical power to detect small age-related effects due to sample size; potential for selection bias as individuals with severe symptoms who could not be scanned were excluded.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: The main limitations of the present study stem from the technical differences in acquisition, which include the aforementioned 1.5 T and 3 T /uniFB01 elds... Our power to observe age-related differences was constrained by sample size... Results may not generalize to 16p11.2 CNV carriers with extreme obesity or severe ASD symptoms that were unable to complete the scanning session.
